And in his place arose Ismail, the son of his brother's son,
and he took as a wife the wife of Ya'qub Arslan himself,
who was the daughter of the Sultan.
And Nur al-Din encamped against Harim.
Then five leaders assembled:
the Prince of Antioch,
and the Count of Tripoli,
and Thoros of Cilicia,
and the Greek Dux of Tarsus,
and the Master {OCR?} of the Hospitallers,
and with them about thirteen thousand horsemen and foot soldiers.
And they came and met Nur al-Din,
and the Franks were grievously defeated.
And the Count, the Dux, and the Prince were captured,
and they were taken as prisoners to Aleppo.
And the Hospitallers were all killed.
And Thoros escaped to Antioch.
And the Patriarch of the Franks made great mourning,
and he broke the semantra (church-bells),
and they suspended {or: he suspended} the prayers.
And Nur al-Din took Harim and the Monastery of Dayr Sim'an of the Greeks,
and made the monks slaves, along with the inhabitants of the whole district.
In this year, which is 559
[559 of the Arabs?],
Nur al-Din sent the emir Asad al-Din Shirkuh, the brother of Najm al-Din Ayyub, the father of Saladin, to Egypt.
For these two brothers,
Shirkuh and Ayyub, the sons of Shadhi,
were from the country of Dvin, a city of Armenia,
Kurds by descent.
And they had been in the service of Mujahid al-Din Bihruz the eunuch, the emir of Tikrit, who was a lover of Christians.
And when Shirkuh killed one of the Christians of Tikrit who was very dear to the emir,
both of them fled to Zengi at Mosul,
and he received them,
and they grew great in his service.
And when that Zengi took Baalbek,
he placed Najm al-Din Ayyub there as governor in its fortress.
And when Zengi was killed,
he surrendered the fortress to the lord of Damascus.
And Asad al-Din Shirkuh, his brother, was in the service of Nur al-Din,
and he gave him Homs and Rahbah.
And Ayyub also helped and surrendered Damascus to Nur al-Din,
and they were held in great honor by him.
And when the occasion arose to send troops to Egypt,
since the Egyptians had fallen into dispute,
and Shawar, the vizier of Egypt, came and requested aid,
